ADIB page 4 reports consolidated total profit of EGP7,550,833 thousand; dividing by 1,000 gives EGP7,550.833 million. ORAS page 8 reports consolidated total profit of USD127.8 million. These figures refer to the same six-month end date but remain in different currencies. Their raw magnitudes cannot support a ranking or sum; no appropriate FX rate or translation convention is supplied. An income-flow comparison normally needs a consistent period translation basis, not an arbitrary current spot quote.

Even after currency normalization, bank funding margins, leverage, credit losses and capital needs differ from construction project margins, working-capital conversion and contract risks. Absolute profit can reflect scale rather than attractiveness. Both are positive earnings observations, a useful counterweight to an automatically bearish view, but neither proves sustainable returns on equity or cheapness. Both requested figures include non-controlling interests; attributable profit would be needed for an ordinary shareholder comparison. Need comparable capital employed/equity, sustainable earnings adjustments, cash conversion, FX basis, share counts and contemporaneous valuations. Decision: preserve the normalized numbers separately, investigate sector-specific quality, and refuse a cross-currency investment ranking or aggregate profit calculation until the missing basis is explicit.
